A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEB research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching proofs moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM alignment experiments, out-of-domain evaluations, sampling-diversity measurements and bonus-strength sensitivity results in Section 5, Tables 3–5 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds response-selection ablations, semantic-coherence measurements, bandit simulations and repeated-run summaries.

M1.justification: The GEB objective, three functional instantiations in Table 2, iterative training procedure in Algorithm 1 and restriction to rejected responses are retained. Expanded formulation details and the new all-response ablation do not establish a change to the proposed implementation.

E1.justification: RLHFlow-UltraFeedback training, UltraFeedback evaluation, AlpacaEval2 and MATH-500 coverage remain unchanged. V3 Appendix E adds a synthetic 1000-arm bandit scenario whose optimal action initially has very low probability, providing a limited extension beyond the retained LLM tasks.

E2.justification: The external baseline membership in Tables 3–4 is unchanged, including the KL-only comparisons with SELM, XPO and VPO. New Table 6 evaluates all-response versions of the three GEB variants against their retained rejected-only implementations, adding a limited set of comparison variants.

E3.justification: The main LLM training and evaluation settings are retained. Added analyses introduce all-versus-rejected response controls, GPT-4 coherence scoring from 0 to 3 on final-iteration responses, and a bandit protocol with 5000 iterations, 64 rollouts and 32 preference pairs per iteration.

E4.justification: V1's sampling-distribution, distinct-n and bonus-strength analyses are retained. V3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Table 6 tests the rejected-only implementation choice, Table 7 checks whether exploration produces incoherent outputs, and Appendix E tests escape from a deliberately constructed local optimum.

E5.justification: V1 reports empirical point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. V3 Appendix F.1 and Table 8 newly report three-run means and standard deviations for f-DPO, FEB and GEB across both backbones and all three divergences. This does not establish a one-to-three increase in runs. No significance test is specified, and checklist item 7 contradicts the added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 3–5 and Figures 2–3 retain their results. V3 adds all-response ablation scores, coherence scores, repeated-run summaries and bandit outcomes. For example, Table 6 reports KL GEB-π win rates of 79.78 with all responses versus the retained 81.00 with rejected responses; Figure 4 reports recovery of the rare optimal action. These expand the evidence without changing the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and regret rate remain. Local mathematical revisions include specifying the historical sampling-policy construct in Definition 3.1, correcting the reward expression to include beta times log Z, and invoking monotonicity rather than positivity in Theorem 3.3's proof. Assumption C.1 no longer explicitly bounds the transformed reward R(r). The relocated proofs already existed in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: failure of prior theoretical bonuses, GEB's optimism guarantee and unification of heuristic bonuses, and empirical benefits across divergence families and LLM backbones. The additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds localized interpretations: rejected-only bonuses are asserted to preserve optimism because rejected responses occupy low-reference-probability regions; coherence results are interpreted as exploration of meaningful underrepresented outputs; and Appendix F.2 connects greater convexity of u to more conservative probability shifts. These explanations were absent from v1, while the central mechanism interpretation remains.

D1.justification: The main hardware, hyperparameters, Algorithm 1 and public code link are retained. Appendix E newly documents the bandit's parameterization, training budget, batch construction, learning rate and lack of warm-up. The added checklist also supplies an anonymous code-access link alongside the retained public link.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and Appendix A's broad positioning remain unchanged. V3 more explicitly contrasts GEB with elliptical-potential, Bayesian and epistemic-network uncertainty estimation on computational grounds, and Appendix B.3 elaborates XPO's dependence on a KL-specific implicit-Q relation.

P1.justification: Sections 2–4 undergo extensive explanatory rewriting, with expanded policy definitions and new boxed implications and takeaways. Proofs from the main text and v1 Appendix E are consolidated into v3 Appendix B. V3 removes standalone end statements, adds experimental appendices and appends a NeurIPS checklist, substantially changing exposition and organization.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 6–8 and Figures 4–5, relocates retained experimental displays and revises captions, including Figure 1 and Table 2. The NeurIPS template changes the title treatment, running headers, headings and page composition, while new boxed passages and a text-wrapped coherence table materially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves empirical scrutiny through repeated-run uncertainty, direct testing of the rejected-only implementation, a coherence check and a controlled exploration example. These address gaps in v1's supporting evidence while retaining its main results. The gain is limited by unsupported statistical-significance assertions, a contradictory checklist response and unresolved checklist references; the revision does not establish a comprehensive strengthening of the theoretical guarantees.
